summary: Pedro Rodrigues, AI tooling engineer at Supabase, presents lessons from building the Supabase agent skill, announced during this talk. He notes the MCP-versus-skills debate has settled—both have distinct roles—and focuses on how skills provide the guidance agents need when working with products updated after their training data. Supabase observed agents missing security pitfalls like row-level security (RLS) instructions, operating on stale knowledge, and being reluctant to seek fresh information. He defines skills as folders containing instructions, scripts, and resources with a front matter envelope (name, description) that agents discover progressively, a main skill.md file, and optional bundled reference files. A key test compared the same agent (Claude Sonnet 4.6) with MCP alone versus MCP plus the skill, tasked with creating a SQL view over an RLS-enabled table. Without the security_invoker=true flag, Postgres views bypass RLS. The MCP-only agent shipped an unsafe query; the skill-equipped agent did not. He shares three principles: don't duplicate documentation—point agents to the single source of truth and be persistent about making them search; if something can be skipped, it will—agents are reluctant to load reference files, so critical information like security checklists must go directly in skill.md; and be opinionated—guide agents to the workflows you know work best, such as Supabase's schema management approach using direct DDL on staging, an advisor check, then migration creation. Supabase also announced exposing documentation through SSH, letting agents navigate docs like a file system. Evals ran six scenarios across four agents from two vendors (Claude Code with Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6, Codex with GPT 5.4 and GPT 5.4 mini) in three conditions: baseline, MCP only, and MCP plus skill. Skills plus MCP outperformed all other conditions on every model. In a closing Q&A, Pedro addressed vector database demand—customers increasingly explore embeddings and semantic search, with potential to augment SSH docs navigation with semantic search. On skill distribution, he acknowledged it remains an unsolved industry problem: Vercel introduced a skills package, plugins can bundle with MCP servers but are model-specific, and internally Supabase packages skills inside repos (dot Claude plugin, dot cursor plugin) that are discoverable when open-sourced. The bottom line: it's guidance, not context, that makes agents reliable.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

sections.title: Introduction and Title Change
sections.summary: Pedro explains the title changed because the MCP vs skills debate has settled; both have distinct roles. He introduces the talk as lessons learned from writing the Supabase skill, noting it was the most complex document he has written since his master thesis.

sections.title: Speaker Introduction
sections.summary: Pedro introduces himself as an AI tooling engineer at Supabase, MCP enthusiast, and co-founder of Lisbon AI Week. He switches to dark mode for the presentation.

sections.title: Agents Need Guidance
sections.summary: Agents are smart but need guidance for tasks involving products updated after training. Supabase noticed agents miss security pitfalls like RLS, rely on stale knowledge, and resist seeking fresh information.

sections.title: Skills Overview
sections.summary: Skills are folders with instructions, scripts, and resources that agents discover progressively. They have front matter (name, description), a main skill.md file, and optional bundled reference files that don't load immediately to context.

sections.title: MCP vs MCP Plus Skill Test
sections.summary: Tested Claude Sonnet 4.6 creating a SQL view over an RLS-enabled table. Without security_invoker=true, Postgres views bypass RLS and expose data. MCP-only agent shipped unsafe query; MCP plus skill agent succeeded.

sections.title: Supabase Agent Skill Announcement
sections.summary: Pedro announces the Supabase agent skill and live tweets it on stage.

sections.title: Principles for Writing Skills
sections.summary: Three principles: don't duplicate documentation—point to single source of truth; critical info goes in skill.md because agents skip reference files; be opinionated about best workflows like Supabase's DDL-then-advisor-then-migration schema workflow. Also announces SSH documentation exposure as a remote file system for agents.

sections.title: Evals and Results
sections.summary: Ran 6 scenarios across 4 agents from 2 vendors in 3 conditions using Braintrust. Skills plus MCP outperformed all other conditions on every model tested.

sections.title: Conclusion and Giveaway
sections.summary: Takeaways: point to single source of truth, be opinionated, start minimal. Blog post is live with install commands. Mac mini giveaway via QR code.

sections.title: Q&A: Vector Databases and Skill Distribution
sections.summary: Pedro fields questions. On vector databases: customers increasingly explore embeddings and semantic search, with potential to augment SSH docs navigation with semantic search. On skill distribution: it's an unsolved industry problem—Vercel's skills package exists, plugins can bundle with MCP but are model-specific; internally Supabase packages skills in repos via dot Claude or dot cursor plugin files, discoverable when open-sourced. A brief exchange about self-improving skills leads to a collab invitation.
